Jobs, fellowships, courses and calls

Uppsala University seeks a permanent senior lecturer in Hindi

The full-time post in the Department of Linguistics and Philology centres on teaching Hindi to undergraduates. Applications close on 11 January 2027.

Talaash Heritage desk · Published 11 November 2026

Where
Uppsala, Sweden
Apply by
11 January 2027

Uppsala University in Sweden has advertised a permanent, full-time post of Senior Lecturer in Hindi in its Department of Linguistics and Philology, part of the Faculty of Languages. The advertisement says the post starts with a temporary contract and that a trial period may apply. The start date is as soon as possible or by agreement.

The work is mainly undergraduate teaching of Hindi, along with course development, supervising and examining theses, course administration and taking part in the department's research and seminars. Administrative or leadership duties may be added.

Applicants need a doctorate in Indology or another relevant language subject, or equivalent expertise, and documented ability to teach Hindi at university level. They also need at least ten weeks of higher-education teaching training or the equivalent, which in special cases can be completed within the first two years. Teaching may be in English or Swedish to begin with, but the holder is expected to be able to teach in Swedish within two years.

In assessment the university will weigh both scholarly and teaching merit, giving special weight to research in Hindi studies and Indology and to documented ability to teach Hindi. Teaching experience in Indology and Sanskrit counts in a candidate's favour.

Applications are made in English through the university's online system under reference UFV-PA 2026/2814, by 11 January 2027. They should include a covering letter, CV, a research plan and a plan for developing Hindi teaching (each up to three pages), accounts of scholarly, teaching and leadership merits, a list of publications, up to ten selected works and degree certificates. The Head of Department, Mats Dahllöf, answers questions about the post.

Sources
